overview: White develops modestly with e3, keeping options for d4, c4 or b3 and a bishop on e2 or b2. Black can set up with ...d5, ...e6, ...g6 or ...c5 and reaches an equal game. There is little forcing theory; play depends on which set-up each side chooses.

white_ideas.idea: Develop Be2/O-O or b3/Bb2 and play d4 or c4 when ready
Transpose to a Queen's Gambit, English or Colle-type structure
Keep the position flexible and avoid early commitments

black_ideas.idea: Occupy the centre with ...d5 and ...e6 or ...c5
Equalise with simple development and a central break

typical_structures.structure: Flexible pawn structure that transposes into QGD, Colle, English or Réti-like set-ups

approach.notes: A quiet development move that can transpose; not a specific system beyond name.

level.notes: Little to memorise, but the plans are loose.

character.reason: Quiet development with low risk for either side.

structure.reason: The centre is undecided and transposes widely.

approach.reason: A quiet move order choice; not clearly a system or an offbeat try.

level.reason: Easy to play but plans are not obvious.

plans.reason: No single typical plan from the root.
